scope_boundaries: The new section works on a compact connected Riemann surface with a smooth positive background.
All normalized ideal models, including zero mass, are classified by countably supported positive atomic measures of mass at most A.
The upper-volume formula equals total variation on this ideal-model space and is complete there. Its dense analytic subspace uses positive-mass analytic models.
For every curve potential, the infimum comparison to positive-mass analytic models is its nonatomic polar curvature mass; vanishing is equivalent to equality of ordinary and ideal envelopes.
The diffuse polar example is proved to be an ordinary fixed point directly, without assuming ordinary-envelope idempotence at zero volume.
The earlier complete metric on positive-volume models has different Cauchy sequences near zero mass; no contradiction with equal topology on the positive locus occurs.
No comparison formula or metrization on all ordinary curve models, higher-dimensional zero-volume extension, infinite-mass extension or new background-degeneration result is asserted.
